abstract.t: A COSE Hash Envelope signs the digest of a preimage, not the preimage itself. A verifier that holds the content as a decoded value, such as a CBOR data item, rather than the bytes that were hashed has to encode the value again, and nothing in the Hash Envelope says how the producer encoded it. CBOR permits more than one encoding of the same data item, so a digest mismatch cannot tell a modified value from a value encoded another way. This document defines a COSE Hash Envelope protected-header parameter in which the producer states the deterministic encoding it applied. It defines one value, the integer 1, for the Core Deterministic Encoding Requirements of RFC 8949, and no encoding of its own; an application profile can identify another encoding by a URL. A verifier ignores a value that does not identify an encoding it implements.
